reasons: Declared 200 schema types test_plans_execution_trend_graph as a bare {type:object} placeholder with no properties.
Actual response is an ARRAY of {name, data} series objects — container mismatch (object declared, array returned).
Each series' data is itself an array of 2-element POSITIONAL tuples [date_string, count], not objects with named fields — same family as get_closed_test_runs_info_v1 and get_issues_count_info_v1.
Exercised on preprod with one real datapoint (['2026-09-17', 1]) on a plan chosen specifically because it was one of only two plans with any activity.

setup.why: resolve a plan with real, substantial trend history
also scope by test_run_id, to check the mutually-exclusive alternate scoping path

secondary_probe_test_run_id_scoping.note: Confirms the mutually-exclusive test_run_id scoping path also works and returns the same {name,data[[...]]} shape; on a 0-test-case run it degrades to a single epoch-anchored zero point rather than an empty array or an error — an edge-case worth knowing about but not itself a contract violation (the container/point shape is unchanged).

declared_missing: The declared schema for test_plans_execution_trend_graph is a bare {type:object} with no properties — it does not declare an array, a name/data series shape, or the inner point shape. Same gap on prod as on preprod.
undeclared_returned: name (series label, e.g. "Untested"/"Failed" — a result-status name, undocumented)
data (per-series array of [date_string, count_int] positional pairs, undocumented)

notes: PREPROD VERDICT REPRODUCES, and this time with real high-volume production data rather than a single deliberately-chosen datapoint on a mostly-empty fixture. Plan 181340 (Test Plan - 10/08/2026, 16,432 total statuses) returns a real 5-point time series across two named series (Untested, Failed) — both series use the exact same declared-object/actual-array container mismatch and the exact same positional [date,count] point shape preprod found. This is a stronger confirmation than preprod's single-point check: the positional-array bug is not an edge-case artifact of a nearly-empty plan, it is the shape for a genuinely populated, weeks-long trend on a project with 16k+ test cases. The test_run_id-scoped variant (mutually exclusive with test_plan_id) was also exercised and shows the same container/point shape, degrading gracefully to a single epoch-anchored zero point on a 0-case run rather than erroring or returning an empty array — worth noting for anyone consuming this on a fresh/empty run, but not a new defect. No 400 for missing/both ids was tested here (out of scope for this recheck — already documented and not part of the DRIFT verdict being rechecked).
